correctness.rationale: The physical comparison fixes the three clocks at the same marginal rate. Conditional Poisson-partition independence gives an exact mixed Binomial(3,p) rank law. Convexity of the Brownian hitting CDF up to d^2/(6D) makes the short-time Jensen comparison strict. Renewal equations produce two unique positive poles, their strictly separated exponents by Cauchy–Schwarz, and the third-survival negligible remainder by a positive exponential moment; the nonlattice key renewal theorem supplies the precise coefficients. All domain restrictions, scaling and tail limits are explicit. 154 supplementary checks execute from the packaged verifier.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-record and literature checks found no matched rigorous opposite-sign time comparison for the three-searcher middle arrival. The closest 2026 paper studies independent-clocks exact rank reference and reset-protocol optimal-rate profiles; 2023 fastest-hitting results and a 2020 single-completion median result do not imply this theorem. Jensen and renewal machinery are acknowledged methods. Residual full-supplement and general-law priority risks remain; this is not independent certification.
residual_risks: The full supplement to arxiv:2609.23542 was not retrievable on repeated web requests; an unstated exact CDF result there would change the priority assessment.
Some older highly relevant primary sources were accessible only as public abstracts, leaving limited full-text comparison.
General theorems on marked renewal or common-environment counts could conceivably imply the specific middle-arrival inversion. No literature-wide priority certification is claimed.

value.rationale: Three labels are the minimal population admitting an interior rank, not an arbitrary numeric cut. Exact short/long reversal proves a qualitative obstruction to universal first-passage protocol preference despite matching all one-body marginals. It supplies a sharp asymptotic hazard-rate separation and a reproducible quantitative benchmark for rank-dependent resetting experiments; no large downstream theorem is needed to make this structural result useful.
